subject: Getting unusual fitted values in a simple model

messages.author: 2fa1b8a933bc31e0
messages.subject: Getting unusual fitted values in a simple model
parts:
Hi,

Currently I am trying to fit a spatial-temporal model with count data in inla with data over a five year period. When fitting a simple model with only a besag spatial term and no temporal terms, I checked the fitted values for each year at the first location to check if they were all the same but they were slightly different at each year. The fitted values from the inla model were only different by a few decimal places for each year at each area but should have all been the same as it would have been using the same intercept and spatial term for that specific area. The spatial terms were the same value at each area over the five year period so I am unsure of what might be causing these strange fitted values. 

This model also an unusual warning message that did not appear with other models fitted with inla that had more than one term in them. Any ideas on what might be causing this? 

Here is the code and warning given
formula1 <-  y ~ f(NO, model="besag", graph = W)
 inla(formula1, family="poisson",data=data, control.compute=list(dic=1))

*** Warning *** Numerical error gives b22 = -17298.6 <= 0.0 for idx=1626. setting b22=1.49167e-154
*** Warning *** Numerical error gives b22 = -73990.9 <= 0.0 for idx=1626. setting b22=1.49167e-154


Craig

Hi

about the predictions (which I think you mean the 'fitted.values'), then
I guess the answer is here:

http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-How-can-I-do-predictions-using-INLA-

and that

control.compute=list(link=1)

is what you want.

about the 'b22' problem, then this is something that should not happen,
as mathematically b22 > 0... so its a numerical problem. so it might be
that the model is ill-conditioned and you might need to regularlize it
or modify it to make it more stable. if you want you can send me code++
so I can rerun it here and I can check this for you.
